findings.rationale: Manual review found no Run4 AI BR equivalent to the Section 12.1 Segment 100 field-position sequence. AI BRs :548 and :549 refer to Communications Test message framing and have no segment assignment. AI BR :1957 concerns repeated totals ordered by card type, a different behavior; its six linked cases have generic well-formedness and field-format assertions and do not verify Segment 100 field order.
findings.searchScope: Run4 approved requirement catalog (5,153 AI BRs), with focused full-catalog searches for field order, ordering, position, and sequence language, followed by source and chain review of the closest candidates.

aiTeamFeedback.message: Run4 manual search found no equivalent BR for Segment 100 field order. The generic Communications Test order statements have no segment assignment; the Totals card-type ordering BR is a different behavior. Please add or identify an explicit BR and executable order assertion for Segment 100 fields 1-17, respecting permitted omission of trailing optional fields.

findings.testRuleTitle: TCP/IP message length uses following payload length
findings.rationale: Manual review of the Run4 approved BR catalog found no requirement for the TCP/IP header length to count the following payload, include the TPDU area, and exclude the two length bytes. The closest BRs describe variable Electronic Mail content and a maximum Financial Transaction Request size; their linked cases contain no TCP/IP header and only generic response/field-format assertions.
findings.searchScope: Run4 approved requirement catalog (5,153 AI BRs), focused full-catalog searches for message framing, following payload length, TPDU inclusion, and length-field exclusion, followed by review of the two closest BR chains and physical payloads.

aiTeamFeedback.message: Run4 manual search found no equivalent BR or executable test for TCP/IP Message Length. Please add or identify a BR and test that calculate the two-byte header value from the following payload, including TPDU bytes but excluding the two-byte length field.

findings.testRuleTitle: TCP/IP message length uses network byte order
findings.rationale: Manual review of the Run4 approved BR catalog found no requirement or executable assertion for Message Length byte order. The closest BRs describe variable Electronic Mail content and a maximum Financial Transaction Request size; their linked cases contain no TCP/IP header and only generic response/field-format assertions. ATL105 Appendix A is internally inconsistent: its table says network/big-endian, a following sentence says network/little-endian, while the 0x1234 example sends 0x12 before 0x34.
findings.searchScope: Run4 approved requirement catalog (5,153 AI BRs), focused full-catalog searches for endian, byte-order, and network-order wording, followed by review of the two closest BR chains, physical payloads, and Appendix A text.

aiTeamFeedback.message: Run4 manual search found no equivalent BR or executable test for TCP/IP Message Length byte order. Please add or identify the explicit byte-order requirement and test. The source itself conflicts (table and example indicate big-endian; following prose says little-endian), so confirm the intended behavior with the specification owner before asserting it.

findings.rationale: AI BR :1511 states the Data Section 1 field-separator boundaries for Totals Request; :1674 states Data Section 1 boundaries for CA Public Key File Load plus other fields. The AI artifacts are structured JSON content, so literal Field Separator bytes are converter responsibility and their absence from JSON is not an AI-output defect. There is still an AI chain/content gap: TC-018521 payloads Totals Request segments without Data Section 1 elements and its scenario SC-8451 points to requirement :1512, not :1511; TC-018599 payloads a generic Financial Transaction Request without Data Section 1 content or CA Public Key Load Segment 132 and its scenario SC-8614 points to :1675, not :1674. Both cases assert generic well-formedness and field character-type/length only. Thus the candidate BRs are relevant, but neither linked chain demonstrates the corresponding Data Section 1 JSON content under the correct requirement; actual separator-byte placement remains unassessed at the converter boundary.
findings.searchScope: Run4 approved requirement catalog (5,153 AI BRs), focused separator/field-boundary search, source comparison against ATL105 Section 11.1.1, and review of both linked scenario IDs, test-case metadata, physical payloads, and assertion lists.

aiTeamFeedback.message: Run4 contains relevant Data Section 1 separator BR statements (:1511 and :1674), but the generated chains are mislinked to neighboring scenario requirements and the linked JSON cases do not carry the matching Data Section 1 content. Please correct the BR-to-scenario links and ensure the JSON carries the appropriate Data Section 1 field values. Do not place literal Field Separator bytes in the AI JSON; verify separator encoding separately at the converter boundary, preserving separators for empty fields and the source-permitted trailing-omission rule.

findings.testRuleTitle: Segment Length represents encoded Segment 100 content
findings.rationale: Run4 candidate BR :5036 states that Segment Length equals the sum of segment data-element lengths plus related Field Separators and Product Data Field Delimiters, making it a strong semantic candidate for R-016. Its source-anchor mapping uses element-parent inference across 42 segment contexts and remains REVIEW_REQUIRED_AMBIGUOUS_OR_COMPOSITE_CANDIDATE, so it does not establish a Segment 100-scoped match. Candidate :090 states only numeric format and a four-byte maximum; it omits the encoded-length calculation. The 144 :090 case links include 16 cases marked approvedInProducerCatalog, but none has specific assertion evidence; 28 cases have some ASSERT evidence, all outside that approved subset. The available Segment Length expected-response entries are INFER/format_only with null values, not calculated-length oracles. Candidate :5036 has six linked rows, all unapproved and without specific assertions. The other linked statements (:3762 and :4831) describe metadata/catalog status, not the required length behavior. AI test data is structured JSON message content, not serialized wire bytes: the SegmentLength key/value should be correct and its calculated value must logically account for required Field Separators, but literal separator bytes are converter responsibility and must not be required in the AI JSON. The available Run4 evidence does not show an approved assertion validating the SegmentLength JSON value against the represented Segment 100 fields. Actual separator-byte serialization can be assessed separately at the converter boundary. Structural links do not establish R-016 test coverage.
findings.searchScope: Run4 approval-independent crosswalk population (5,153 AI BRs); all four R-016 candidate pairs (:090, :3762, :4831, :5036); direct case-register rows, producer approval flags, expected-response tiers, physical request metadata, and candidate chain mappings. No AI source artifacts or local sessions were modified.

aiTeamFeedback.message: Run4 includes a source-text candidate (:5036) stating the Segment Length calculation, but its inferred Element 84 mapping spans 42 segment contexts and its six linked cases are unapproved with no specific assertions. The :090 requirement only checks numeric/maximum-width formatting; none of its 16 producer-approved cases has a targeted assertion, and the expected Segment Length responses are INFER/format_only. Please scope an approved BR and test chain to Segment 100 and validate that the AI JSON SegmentLength value equals the derived length of its represented Segment 100 content, logically counting each required Field Separator without embedding literal separator bytes in JSON. Add a wrong-length value mutation. Test actual separator-byte encoding separately at the converter boundary; do not treat a calculation placeholder as execution evidence.

findings.rationale: The Section 12.1 source says all Segment 100 fields are separated by a Field Separator and that separators remain for unpopulated fields. AI BR :1709 repeats that behavior and is a strong semantic candidate. Per the established artifact boundary, the AI JSON represents message content and field values; it is not the serialized ATL105 byte stream. Therefore literal Field Separators are not expected in the AI JSON, and their absence there is not an AI-output defect. Converter-side serialization must add and validate separator placement. The six linked Run4 cases are unapproved. TC-008362 carries a low-confidence ASSERT ('Transmit a Field Separator for that field position', confidence 0.31), but no authorized converter-side wire observation is provided, so converter behavior remains unassessed. Other lexical hits :1708, :1917, and :1940 concern trailing optional omission or special Prompt Code 902/904 formats and are not interchangeable with the general empty-field rule.
findings.searchScope: ATL105 Section 12.1 source, Serialization triage candidates :1708, :1709, :1917, and :1940, the Run4 approval-independent BR crosswalk, six linked case-register rows, expected-response metadata, and converter/wire evidence boundary. JSON content was not treated as serialized wire evidence.

aiTeamFeedback.message: Run4 BR :1709 states the separator rule, but its six linked cases are unapproved and converter-side wire behavior is not established. The AI JSON is message content, not a wire message, so do not add literal Field Separators to the AI output or treat their absence as a defect. Preserve valid field values and empty/omitted-field semantics in JSON; validate separator encoding at the converter boundary with an approved wire fixture and targeted assertion.

findings.testRuleTitle: Run4 AI candidates represent the corrected Visa transaction-flow inventory
findings.rationale: Compared the corrected Credit Visa/BuyPass list of 14 flow shapes against the 89 Run4 case-register entries marked isFlow=true, their sidecars, and declared JSON legs. No standalone Run4 flow candidate was found for Authorization or Sale; no matching candidate was found for COF/MIT or the report-only Unclassified bucket; and no exact Authorization -> Completion -> Timeout candidate was found. Run4 candidates do exist for Authorization -> Completion (TC-006448), Authorization -> Void (TC-006490), Sale -> Void (TC-006502), Refund -> Void (TC-006472), a generic financial transaction -> Time-out Reversal (TC-006478), Authorization -> Cancellation (TC-006484), Authorization -> Partial Completion (TC-006454), Authorization -> Completion -> Void (TC-006496), and Authorization -> Completion -> Duplicate Completion (TC-006460). The generic timeout candidate does not identify its original request as a Sale. Separately, the Run4 Segment 100 suite catalog reports 16 declared flows, 0 generated flows, 16 skipped flows, 1,650 single-leg cases, and 0 multi-leg cases. An exhaustive scan of all 4,844 Run4 Segment 100 TC cards found no expected Response Code 2 or 3. ATL105 defines these as Approved Authorization Only and Approved Authorization Only with AVS, respectively. Response Code 0 means Approved Purchase/Capture and is not evidence of an approved Authorization Only flow. Scenario expectations tell a different, unvalidated story: each of the byte-identical Run2, Run3, and Run4 approved-scenario catalogs contains 4,224 records with expected_response_code 2, zero with code 3, and all 4,224 are typed negative; 82 target Auth Completion (0220). Their oracle_authority is Level C, chatbot-sourced. Run1 has no standalone scenario catalog. Do not count these unvalidated negative scenario defaults as positive Authorization Only evidence, especially because no corresponding TC card expects code 2 or 3. Separate independent Test Solution package segment-100-response-code-package.json contains one BR covering codes 2 and 3 together (BR-SEG100-RC-APPROVED-AUTH), with one TS/TC and one ResponseCode 2 TD; the TD expectedValidation is REVIEW and there is no separate ResponseCode 3 TD. This is a Test Solution artifact, not Run4 AI coverage or an execution-certified result. The cited isFlow=true cases have empty requirementIds and structuralStatus NO_BR_ATTRIBUTION; their register verificationStatus PASS is not proof of transaction acceptance or execution.
findings.searchScope: Run1-Run4 same-date Segment 100 TC cards (4,844 per run); Run2-Run4 approved_scenarios.json (14,297 scenarios each; SHA-256 identical); Run1 absence of standalone scenario-generation catalog; Run4 analysis-v2 case register, all 89 isFlow=true records and sidecars; suite catalog; independent response-code package; ATL105 Response Code family matrix; and corrected Visa flow inventory. Scenario expected-response values and TC-card expected-response rows were counted separately.

scenarioResponseCodeAudit.coverageInterpretation: Unvalidated negative scenario expectations; not positive Authorization Only flow or TC coverage.

aiTeamFeedback.message: Please add or identify explicit Run4 BR -> TS -> TC -> TD chains for standalone Authorization and Sale, and for the exact Authorization -> Completion -> Timeout sequence if supported by ATL105. The Segment 100 suite catalog says 16 flows were declared, 0 generated and 16 skipped; all 1,650 generated cases are single-leg. An exhaustive scan of 4,844 Segment 100 TC cards found no expected response code 2 or 3, which ATL105 defines as Approved Authorization Only and Approved Authorization Only with AVS. Separately, the byte-identical Run2, Run3, and Run4 scenario catalogs each assign expected_response_code 2 to 4,224 negative scenarios (82 target Auth Completion), assign code 3 to none, and label the oracle authority Level C/chatbot-sourced. These unvalidated scenario defaults conflict with the TC-card expected-response rows and must not be counted as approved Authorization Only cases; please review and correct the expected-response assignments. Code 0 means Approved Purchase/Capture, not Authorization Only. The independent Test Solution response-code package has one BR covering both codes, but only a ResponseCode 2 fixture; its outcome is REVIEW, not PASS, and there is no separate code-3 TD. Please add source-grounded positive Authorization Only cases for code 2 and code 3-with-AVS, plus appropriate negative cases, and link them through BR -> TS -> TC -> TD. Add a COF/MIT flow only with its stored-credential context and source-backed behavior. Unclassified is a report fallback label, not a defined transaction flow; map its underlying case to a real flow or keep it out of the flow inventory. For existing multi-leg candidates, add direct BR attribution and leg-specific TD/assertion evidence. In particular, either specialize TC-006478 to prove Sale -> Timeout or label it as a generic financial transaction -> Time-out Reversal case. Do not count starter Test Solution mappings or Run4 structural verification status as AI flow coverage.

findings.testRuleTitle: Field order matches Section 12.2 (base fields 1-13, Auth Completion tag fields 14-18)
findings.rationale: ATL105 Section 12.2 lays out Segment 101 base fields 1-13 in order and Fleet Tag 1-5 at fields 14-18 for Auth Completion messages. A search of the complete 5,153-row Run4 AI BR crosswalk found no AI BR stating or asserting that Segment 101 field sequence. The closest BRs are not equivalent: :1737 addresses Field Separators, :1738 says Fleet Tags 1-5 are sent only in Auth Completion, :1739 covers valid tag codes/Host Prompt applicability, and :2229-:2233 cover individual Fleet Tag presence conditions. Their linked cases have no field-order assertion. The six :1737 cases assert separators at confidence 0.31; the :1738 and :1739 cases assert lifecycle/tag-code constraints; the per-tag presence cases test presence, not position. A structured JSON object's property order is not evidence of converter wire order. This is a Run4-specific no-equivalent finding, not a global absence claim or a confirmed AI_ONLY classification.
findings.searchScope: Approval-independent Run4 population (all 5,153 AI BRs), explicit searches for field-order/field-sequence wording, Fleet Segment field numbers 1-13 and Fleet Tag fields 14-18, Auth Completion tag ordering, full-text review of nearest Fleet statements, and inspection of their linked scenario/case assertions and approval statuses.

aiTeamFeedback.message: Manual Run4 search found no AI BR that states the Segment 101 field order (base fields 1-13, then Fleet Tags 1-5 at fields 14-18 in Auth Completion). Nearby BRs cover separators, tag presence/applicability, or tag-code values, not order; their cases do not assert field sequence. Please add or identify an independently grounded BR and a test chain that checks the Segment 101 field order and Auth Completion tag extension. Do not use JSON property ordering as proof of serialized wire order; validate converter wire order separately if the converter is in scope.
